descriptions.autopilot: Runs the task to the end on its own, asking only when it genuinely cannot proceed.
descriptions.checkpoints: Plans the work in stages and briefs you after each one, then keeps going on its own. Asks only at genuine forks.
descriptions.interrogate: Asks 2–4 important questions before a new task, waits for answers, then carries out the agreed scope without repeating questions.
descriptions.build: Builds the whole project in one flight: requirements taken from your own words, tickets in parallel, a final check against the brief. Progress lives on the Autopilot tab. With permissions bypassed it asks nothing at all.

firstTask.title: What to do with these files
firstTask.subtitle: Tap a job — questions arrive as buttons. The brief is for the agent, you do not send anything.
firstTask.claudeNeeded: Sign in to Claude first — otherwise the agent cannot work.
firstTask.briefPreamble:
This is a BRIEF, not “just make something”.
Hard order:
1) Skim the project files — what already exists. Do not re-ask facts that are already in the files. Do NOT draft anything yet.
2) Ask clarifying questions with AskUserQuestion (or ask_user_question). Options as buttons, not a numbered list in chat. First batch: 5–7 questions. Each question closes a decision that would change the result. Every question needs a short recommended option in the description plus “you decide / I don’t know”. Do not ask the obvious, and do not ask taste (“modern or classic”).
3) STOP. Wait for answers. No files, pages, posts, or tables until they answer.
4) If a hole remains that would make you invent a price, a fact, or a reference look — second batch of 2–4 questions. Then stop asking.
5) After answers: 5–8 lines of brief (who it is for, what we make, what we skip, what “done” looks like) and then do the work.
Forbidden: “not much data, I’ll improvise”. No answers — no work. Do not invent prices, reviews, numbers, photos, or other people’s quotes. Missing from files and answers → write “to confirm”.

site.label: Website or landing page
site.prompt:
Job: a sales page or a small site for this business.
Done: on a phone it is clear who this is, one promise, one action; the page can be sent to a client. No invented numbers, reviews, or faces.
Ask with buttons (decisions, not taste). Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— After the visit, what MUST happen: a message lead / a call / a booking / they understood and will write later. I would take a message lead — easiest to check.
— Who opens it and why they do not buy today: they don’t know you / they don’t trust the promise / it feels expensive / they already have someone.
— One promise on the first screen, not four equal pluses: a result / speed / “we’ll figure it for you” / a price — only if it is in the files.
— What proof already exists: reviews or cases in the folder / photos of work / numbers from the files / no proof — write honestly, no fake.
— What it should feel like: name 1–2 sites you know by heart / there is an existing site to redo / you pick a reference from the same world, not “like Apple”.
— What we deliver this round: one page, sendable today / several pages (home, services, contacts) / section copy only, build later.
After answers: 5–8 lines of brief, then the work. Do not invent or generate images — describe what to take from the folder. Do not appoint a reference they did not name.

crm.label: Client tracker
crm.prompt:
Job: a simple client tracker for this business, not enterprise CRM.
Done: a table or a small board where a lead can be added today and the step is visible.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— Who uses this every day: only me on a phone / me and staff / just me for now, a team later. I would start with “only me on a phone” — fewer screens.
— Who a “client” is in real life: an ad lead, not bought yet / already bought / a subscriber, far from a purchase.
— Which deal steps actually exist, not a textbook: new → talking → waiting for payment → done / my own 3–5 steps.
— Where the truth lives now: messenger chat / a sheet / nowhere, all in my head. If it is in the head, the tracker must be shorter than the habit of typing in chat.
— If nobody opened a card for three days: remind me / nothing, I look myself / hand to a staff member.
— What we deliver: a table fillable today / a small board with list and statuses / a one-page map first, the board later.
After answers: fields and stages plus a working draft. Do not invent names, phones, or sums.

bot.label: Messenger bot
bot.prompt:
Job: a bot that takes one routine off the chat.
Done: a flow with buttons and ready message copy. Code only if they ask for it separately.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— Where: Telegram / MAX / both. If unsure, start where clients already write.
— One main job, not three at once: take a lead / answer frequent questions / book a time.
— Where the lead goes the same minute: to me in chat / a table / the tracker, if it already exists.
— When a human must step in: always via an “operator” button / if the bot did not understand / the bot runs alone, no human.
— Tone: short / warm / formal. I would take short — long messages are not read in chat.
— Prices and slots in bot replies: only from files / always write “we’ll confirm” / they will name 2–3 figures in the answers.
After answers: the flow and the copy. No code unless they ask. Do not invent prices or hours.

content.label: Posts and content
content.prompt:
Job: a batch of posts ready to paste into a channel.
Done: title, text, and what is on the image for each post. No corporate speak, no invented numbers.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— Where: Telegram / MAX / VK / several. Several means one meaning, different cuts per platform.
— Who reads and what hurts NOW, not “target audience”: say it in their words / propose from the files / I don’t know — read the folder and offer 2 portraits as buttons.
— What this week sells with one blow: a named service / trust, no sell / a lead in chat.
— Tone: neighbour / calm expert / blunt. If they like a channel, name it — that is the reference.
— How many: 3 as a trial / 7 for a week / 14 for two. I would take 7.
— Which facts may go in the text: only files and answers / carefully, with no numbers / they will add 2–3 facts in the answers.
After answers: the posts. Do not invent client quotes or numbers.

competitors.label: Competitor review
competitors.prompt:
Job: a competitor review you can use to decide how to differ — not praise that “everyone is fine”.
Done: 5 names, comparison on 4–5 points, weak spots, how this business can differ. No flattery.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— Market: city and region / the whole country / online, no geography.
— Compare with: the same / pricier / cheaper / I’ll name 2–3. No names — I find 5 similar and confirm them with buttons.
— What people actually pick you for, not “quality”: price / speed / human feel / range / I’ll say.
— Where to look: sites / ads / socials / all of them.
— Output: a table / a one-page review / ideas for how the offer should differ.
— What must not appear: invented reviews / smoothed-over weaknesses / comparison with world brands not from this life.
After answers: 5 competitors and a verdict. Quotes and numbers only with a source; no source → mark “hypothesis”.

offer.label: Sales proposal
offer.prompt:
Job: one one-page sales proposal.
Done: text that can be sent today. Do not invent a price.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— For: one named client / a template for similar clients / I don’t know, make a template.
— Selling with one blow: one service / a package / turnkey. Not three offers in one file.
— They already know you, or this is cold: they know us / cold / mixed, there is a shared name.
— Money at the bottom: a price from the files / “we’ll quote” / several packages, they will name the range. No figures → write “price to confirm”, do not invent a pretty number.
— What proof already exists: a case in the folder / a review / numbers / no proof, do not invent.
— Tone: short and to the point / longer, with stages. I would take short — long proposals are not finished.
After answers: the proposal.

replies.label: Client replies
replies.prompt:
Job: ready replies to paste into chat.
Done: 8–12 lines for the chosen situations, no “dear customer, thank you for reaching out”.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— Where: WhatsApp / Telegram / MAX / email / several.
— Who writes: the owner / a manager in the company voice.
— Situations to cover (several allowed): new lead / price / timing / “too expensive” / a complaint / all of them.
— Tone: owner, plain / polite neutral / firmer, no sugar.
— May the replies offer a discount: never / yes, inside a range they will name / propose wording with no figure.
— Which facts may be promised: only from files / timing and price always “we’ll confirm” / they will add 2–3 facts.
After answers: the replies. Do not promise a discount, a deadline, or a price that is not in the answers.

spreadsheet.label: Spreadsheet review
spreadsheet.prompt:
Job: read the numbers so it is obvious what to do next week.
Done: plain-language takeaways plus 3 concrete steps. No mash of percentages, no invented figures.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— What the sheet is: sales / leads / ads / stock / I don’t know, find it in the folder.
— One main question to the numbers: where money leaks / what is growing / who to stop selling to / I’ll phrase it.
— Period: last month / quarter / year / whatever is in the file.
— Output: 5 takeaways / takeaways plus what to change next week. I would take the second.
— If none exist: which export to attach — sales / leads / ads — then STOP until the file. Do not invent sample figures.
After answers: the takeaways. No sheet — do not fake a review.

ads.label: Ad copy
ads.prompt:
Job: ad copy ready to run.
Done: 5 short (and long, if asked) with no “best on the market” and no numbers that are not there.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— Where: Direct / VK / Telegram / Avito / several. Several means one meaning, different cuts.
— Who we catch and what hurts now: in their words / propose two portraits from the files as buttons.
— One promise: a result / a price if it exists / speed / “we’ll figure it for you”.
— The ask: write / call / leave a lead.
— How many: 5 short / 5 short and 3 long. I would take both if the platform allows a long text.
— Which facts may go in: only files and answers / no numbers at all / they will add 2–3.
After answers: the copy. Forbidden: “best”, “#1”, and any number that is not in the files or answers.

knowledge.label: Knowledge base
knowledge.prompt:
Job: a short knowledge base from the folder so the same facts are not hunted down again.
Done: a cheat sheet in plain language, gaps marked, not papered over.
Ask with buttons. Every question needs “you decide / I don’t know”:
— For: me / a staff member / the agent answering clients.
— Must include: services / prices / how we work / FAQ / whatever you find.
— If a gap: mark “missing” / stop and ask / do not fill it at all. “Fill carefully” is forbidden.
— Size: one page / several short cards. I would take cards — easier to find.
— Ready client answers, or an internal cheat sheet only.
After answers: the base. Mark gaps. Do not invent prices or rules that are not there.
